item.title: Why You Should Not Fear Volatility
item.description: 市场总是会恢复，即便是在二战期间，在CONVID-19市场也不会真正的崩溃
item.content:encoded:
If you want the upside building wealth, you have to accept volatility and periodic declines that come with it. it’s the price of admission for long term investment success.

If you’re not willing to react with equanimity to a market price decline of 50% two or three times a century you’re not fit to be a common shareholder and you deserve the mediocre result you’re going to get.

换句话说，市场在一个世纪才会出现两到三次完美买入机会，你绝对不应该错过它

期望年回报 = （1+%需要多少恢复到高点）^ （1/几年时间恢复）- 1

pow(1.5,1/5)-1

如果市场已经下跌了 33% 那么需要上涨 50%才能恢复。如果一年内能恢复的话。 你在-30%处买入会在恢复同样点位时获得 50%的回报 哪怕市场 5 年才恢复，你也可以获得 8%的回报

事实上 2008 股灾时，用了 5 年市场才恢复到之前高点。 2020 CONVID-19 时用了 9 个月就恢复到了市场高点。

item.title: 持续买入
item.description: 摆脱朝九晚五后，你的财富就能为你持续奔波。
item.content:encoded:
After you stop working your 9 to 5, your money can keep working for you. 停下你的朝九晚五工作后，你的钱可以继续为你工作。

Conclusion: The Just Keep Buying Rules

Highlight(yellow) - Page 281 · Location 4366 Saving is for the Poor, Investing is for the Rich Find where you are in your financial journey before deciding where to focus your time and energy. If your expected savings are greater than your expected investment income, focus on savings; otherwise focus on investing. If they are similar, focus on both. (Ch. 1) 翻译： 储蓄是为穷人准备的，投资是为富人准备的。在决定将时间和精力集中在哪里之前，先确定你在财务旅程中的位置。如果你的预期储蓄高于预期投资收入，就专注于储蓄；否则就专注于投资。如果两者相似，那就同时关注两者。(第 1 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 281 · Location 4370 Save What You Can Your income and spending are rarely fixed, so your savings rate shouldn’t be fixed either. Save what you can to reduce your financial stress. (Ch. 2) 翻译： 尽可能多地储蓄。你的收入和支出很少是固定的，因此你的储蓄率也不应该固定。尽可能多地储蓄，以减轻你的财务压力。(第 2 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 281 · Location 4373 Focus on Income, Not Spending Cutting spending has its limits, but growing your income doesn’t. Find small ways to grow your income today that can turn into big ways to grow it tomorrow. (Ch. 3) 翻译： 关注收入，而非支出。削减支出有其局限性，但增加收入却没有。找到今天能增加收入的小方法，这些小方法可以转化为明天增加收入的大方法。(第 3 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 281 · Location 4376 Use The 2x Rule to Eliminate Spending Guilt If you ever feel guilty about splurging on yourself, invest the same amount of money into income-producing assets or donate to a good cause. This is the easiest way to have worry-free spending. (Ch. 4) 翻译： 使用“2倍规则”来消除消费内疚感。如果你因为为自己大手大脚消费而感到内疚，就把相同金额的钱投资到产生收入的资产中，或者捐赠给一个公益事业。这是实现无忧消费最简单的方法。(第 4 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 282 · Location 4379 Save at Least 50% of Your Future Raises and Bonuses A little lifestyle creep is okay, but keep it below 50% of your future raises if you want to stay on track. (Ch. 5) 翻译： 至少储蓄未来加薪和奖金的 50%。一点生活方式的膨胀是可以接受的，但如果你想保持正轨，请将其控制在未来加薪的 50% 以下。(第 5 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 282 · Location 4382 Debt Isn’t Good or Bad, It Depends on How You Use It Debt can be harmful in some scenarios and helpful in others. Use debt only when it can be most beneficial for your finances. (Ch. 6) 翻译： 债务并非好或坏，这取决于你如何使用它。债务在某些情况下可能有害，在其他情况下可能很有帮助。只有在它能对你的财务带来最大益处时，才使用债务。(第 6 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 282 · Location 4385 Only Buy a Home When the Time Is Right Buying a home will probably be the biggest financial decision you ever make. As a result, you should only do it when it fits into both your finances and your current lifestyle. (Ch. 翻译： 只有在时机成熟时才买房。买房很可能是你做过的最大财务决定。因此，你应该只在它符合你的财务状况和当前生活方式时才购买。(第 [章])

Highlight(yellow) - Page 282 · Location 4388 When Saving for a Big Purchase, Use Cash Though bonds and stocks may earn you more while you wait, when saving for a wedding, home, or other big purchase, cash is the way to go. (Ch. 8) 翻译： 为大额购买储蓄时，使用现金。尽管债券和股票在等待期间可能会为你赚取更多，但在为婚礼、房屋或其他大额购买储蓄时，现金是最佳选择。(第 8 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 282 · Location 4391 Retirement is About More Than Money Before you decide what to retire from, make sure you know what you want to retire to. (Ch. 9) 翻译： 退休不仅仅是关于金钱。在决定从什么领域退休之前，请确保你知道你想退休到哪里去。(第 9 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 283 · Location 4394 Invest to Replace Your Waning Human Capital with Financial Capital You won’t be able to work forever, so replace your human capital with financial capital before it’s too late. Investing is the best way to accomplish this. (Ch. 10) 翻译： 投资以用金融资本取代衰退的人力资本。你不可能永远工作下去，所以在你为时已晚之前，用金融资本来取代你的人力资本。投资是实现这一目标的最佳方式。(第 10 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 283 · Location 4397 Think Like an Owner and Buy Income-Producing Assets To really grow your income, think like an owner and use your money to buy income-producing assets. (Ch. 11) 翻译： 像主人一样思考，购买产生收入的资产。要真正增加你的收入，请像主人一样思考，并用你的钱去购买产生收入的资产。(第 11 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 283 · Location 4400 Don’t Buy Individual Stocks Buying individual stocks and expecting to outperform is like flipping a coin. You might succeed, but even if you do, how do you know it wasn’t just luck? (Ch. 12) 翻译： 不要购买个股。购买个股并期望跑赢大盘，就像抛硬币一样。你可能会成功，但即使成功了，你怎么知道那不是运气使然呢？(第 12 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 283 · Location 4402 Buy Quickly, Sell Slowly Since most markets are expected to rise over time, buying quickly and selling slowly is the optimal way to maximize your wealth. If you don’t feel comfortable with this, then what you are buying/ selling might be too risky for you. (Ch. 13, 18) 翻译： 快速买入，缓慢卖出。由于大多数市场预计会随时间上涨，快速买入和缓慢卖出是最大化财富的最佳方式。如果你对这种方式感到不适，那么你正在买入/卖出的资产可能对你来说风险太高了。(第 13、18 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 283 · Location 4406 Invest As Often As You Can If you think you can time the market by saving up cash, think again. Even God couldn’t beat dollar-cost averaging. (Ch. 14) 翻译： 尽可能频繁地投资。如果你认为通过积累现金可以择时投资市场，那就再想想。即使是上帝也无法击败美元成本平均法（Dollar-Cost Averaging）。(第 14 章) Note - Page 283 · Location 4409 绝对不可能 翻译： 绝对不可能

Highlight(yellow) - Page 284 · Location 4409 Investing Isn’t About the Cards You Are Dealt, but How You Play Your Hand You will experience periods of good and bad luck throughout your investing career. However, the most important thing is how you behave over the long term. (Ch. 15) 翻译： 投资不在于你被发了什么牌，而在于你如何打牌。在你的投资生涯中，你会经历好运和厄运的时期。然而，最重要的是你在长期内的行为表现。(第 15 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 284 · Location 4412 Don’t Fear Volatility When It Inevitably Comes Markets won’t give you a free ride without some bumps along the way. Don’t forget that you have to experience some downside if you want to earn your upside. (Ch. 16) 翻译： 不要害怕波动性，因为它终将到来。市场不会在没有一些起伏的情况下给你免费的顺风车。不要忘记，如果你想获得上涨的收益，就必须经历一些下跌的波动。(第 16 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 284 · Location 4415 Market Crashes Are (Usually) Buying Opportunities Future returns are usually the highest following major crashes. Don’t be afraid to take advantage of these crashes when they periodically occur. (Ch. 17) 翻译： 市场崩盘通常是（最佳）买入机会。在重大崩盘之后，未来的回报通常是最高的。不要害怕利用这些周期性发生的崩盘。(第 17 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 284 · Location 4418 Fund the Life You Need Before You Risk it for the Life You Want Though this book is called Just Keep Buying, sometimes it’s okay to sell. After all, what’s the point of building your wealth if you don’t do anything with it? (Ch. 18) 翻译： 在将它冒险用于你想要的生命之前，先为你需要的生活提供资金。尽管这本书名为“持续买入”，但有时卖出也是可以的。毕竟，如果你不利用你的财富，那么积累财富有什么意义呢？(第 18 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 284 · Location 4421 Don’t Max Out Your 401( k) Without Considerable Thought The annual benefit of a 401( k) can be less than you think. Before you lock up your money for multiple decades, consider what else you might need it for instead. (Ch. 19) 翻译： 在没有充分考虑的情况下不要将你的 401(k) 额度填满。401(k) 的年度收益可能低于你的预期。在将你的资金锁定数十年之前，请考虑你是否需要用它来满足其他需求。(第 19 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 285 · Location 4424 You’ll Never Feel Rich and That’s Okay No matter how successful you get with your money, there will always be someone with more. If you win the financial game, make sure you don’t lose yourself in the process. (Ch. 20) 翻译： 你永远不会觉得自己是富翁，这没关系。无论你的金钱变得多么成功，总会有人拥有更多。如果你赢得了这场财务游戏，请确保你在过程中没有迷失自我。(第 20 章)

Highlight(yellow) - Page 285 · Location 4428 Time is Your Most Important Asset You can always earn more money, but nothing can buy you more time. (Ch. 21) 翻译： 时间是你最重要的资产。你可以永远赚取更多的钱，但没有什么能为你买到更多的时光。(第 21 章)

Introduction

Highlight(yellow) - Page 9 · Location 118 To build wealth it didn’t matter when you bought U.S. stocks, just that you bought them and kept buying them. It didn’t matter if valuations were high or low. It didn’t matter if you were in a bull market or a bear market. All that mattered was that you kept buying. 翻译： 要积累财富，你买美国股票的时间并不重要，重要的是你买了它们，并且持续买入。估值是高是低并不重要。你处于牛市还是熊市也不重要。唯一重要的是你持续买入。

Highlight(yellow) - Page 10 · Location 124 When I say income-producing assets, I mean those assets that you expect to generate income for you far into the future, even if that income isn’t paid directly to you. This includes stocks, bonds, real estate, and much more. However, the specifics of the strategy are not critically important. 翻译： 当我提到“产生收入的资产”时，我的意思是那些你预期它们能为你在遥远的未来产生收入的资产，即使这些收入不是直接支付给你的。这包括股票、债券、房地产等等。然而，策略的具体细节并不至关重要。

Highlight(yellow) - Page 10 · Location 127 It’s not about when to buy, how much to buy, or what to buy—just to keep buying. 翻译： 关键不在于何时买、买多少，或买什么——只是持续买入。

Highlight(yellow) - 1. Where Should You Start? > Page 13 · Location 171 saving is for the poor and investing is for the rich 翻译： 储蓄是为穷人准备的，投资是为富人准备的。

Highlight(yellow) - 1. Where Should You Start? > Page 15 · Location 207 First, figure out how much you expect to comfortably save in the next year. 翻译： 首先，确定你预计在未来一年内能舒适地储蓄多少。

Highlight(yellow) - 1. Where Should You Start? > Page 15 · Location 210 Next, determine how much you expect your investments to grow in the next year (in dollar terms). 翻译： 接下来，确定你预计你的投资在未来一年内能增长多少（以美元计）。

Highlight(yellow) - 1. Where Should You Start? > Page 15 · Location 213 Finally, compare the two numbers. Which is higher, your expected savings or your expected investment growth? 翻译： 最后，比较这两个数字。是你的预期储蓄更高，还是你的预期投资增长更高？

Highlight(yellow) - 1. Where Should You Start? > Page 15 · Location 215 If your expected savings are higher, then you need to focus more on saving money and adding to your investments. However, if your expected investment growth is higher, then spend more time thinking about how to invest what you already have. If the numbers are close to each other, then you should spend time on both. 翻译： 如果你的预期储蓄更高，那么你需要更多地关注储蓄资金和增加你的投资。然而，如果你的预期投资增长更高，那么就花更多时间思考如何投资你已有的资金。如果这两个数字接近，那么你应该同时关注两者。

I. Saving

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 36 · Location 526 This is why it is so much easier for higher income households to save money—they don’t spend on necessities at the same rate, relative to their income, as lower income households. 翻译： 这就是为什么高收入家庭更容易储蓄——相对于他们的收入而言，他们在必需品上的支出速度不像低收入家庭那样快。 Note - 3. How To Save More > Page 36 · Location 528 储蓄率 翻译： 储蓄率

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 37 · Location 546 “Why Do People Stay Poor?” 翻译： “为什么人们会一直贫穷？”

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 37 · Location 550 “[ We] find that, if the program pushes individuals above a threshold level of initial assets, then they escape poverty, but, if it does not, they slide back into poverty… Our findings imply that large one-off transfers that enable people to take on more productive occupations can help alleviate persistent poverty.” 18 翻译： “[我们]发现，如果该项目将个人推至初始资产的某个门槛水平以上，他们就能摆脱贫困；但如果未达到，他们就会滑回贫困……我们的研究结果表明，那些使人们能够从事更具生产性的职业的大额一次性转移支付，有助于缓解持续的贫困。” 18

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 38 · Location 554 many poor people stay poor not because of their talent/ motivation, but because they are in low-paying jobs that they must work to survive. 翻译： 许多贫困人口之所以保持贫困，并非因为他们的才能/动力不足，而是因为他们从事着必须工作才能生存的低薪工作。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 38 · Location 560 This is why the biggest lie in personal finance is that you can be rich if you just cut your spending. 翻译： 这就是为什么个人理财中最主要的谎言是：只要你削减开支，你就能变得富有。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 39 · Location 577 If you want to save more, the main point is to tighten up where you can, then focus on increasing your income. 翻译： 如果你想储蓄更多，主要原则是尽可能地收紧开支，然后专注于增加你的收入。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 39 · Location 587 Sell Your Time/ Expertise Sell a Skill/ Service Teach People Sell a Product Climb the Corporate Ladder 翻译： 出售你的时间/专业知识；出售一项技能/服务；教导他人；出售一个产品；爬上企业阶梯

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 40 · Location 603 Selling Your Time Summary Pros: Easy to do. Low startup cost. Cons: Time is limited. Doesn’t scale. 翻译： 出售你的时间 总结：优点：容易做。启动成本低。缺点：时间有限。难以规模化。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 41 · Location 618 Selling a Skill/ Service Summary Pros: Higher pay. Able to build a brand. Cons: Need to invest time to develop marketable skill/ service. Doesn’t scale easily. 翻译： 出售一项技能/服务 总结：优点：报酬更高。能够建立品牌。缺点：需要投入时间来培养可销售的技能/服务。难以轻松规模化。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 42 · Location 633 Teaching People Summary Pros: Easily scalable. Cons: Lots of competition. Attracting students can be an ongoing battle. 翻译： 教导他人 总结：优点：易于规模化。缺点：竞争激烈。吸引学生可能是一场持续的战斗。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 42 · Location 639 The best way to do this is to identify a problem and then build a product to solve it. The problem could be emotional, mental, physical, or financial in nature. Whatever you decide on, solving a problem through a product helps you create scalable value. 翻译： 做到这一点最好的方法是识别一个问题，然后构建一个产品来解决它。这个问题可以是情感的、精神的、身体的或财务的。无论你决定什么，通过产品解决问题都能帮助你创造可扩展的价值。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 43 · Location 647 Selling a Product Summary Pros: Scalable. Cons: Lots of upfront investment and constant marketing. 翻译： 出售一个产品 总结：优点：可规模化。缺点：需要大量的前期投资和持续的营销。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 44 · Location 671 Climbing the Corporate Ladder Summary Pros: Gain skills and experience. Less risk around income growth. Cons: You don’t control your time or what you do. 翻译： 爬上企业阶梯 总结：优点：获得技能和经验。收入增长风险较低。缺点：你无法控制你的时间或你做什么。

Highlight(yellow) - 3. How To Save More > Page 44 · Location 676 Regardless of how you try to increase your income in the future, all of the methods above should be viewed as temporary measures. I say temporary because, ultimately, your extra income should be used to acquire more income-producing assets. That’s how you really give your savings a boost. 翻译： 无论你如何尝试在未来增加收入，上述所有方法都应该被视为临时措施。我说它是临时的，是因为最终，你的额外收入应该被用来获取更多的产生收入的资产。这就是你真正给储蓄提供动力的方式。

II. Investing

Bookmark - 10. Why Should You Invest? > Page 114 · Location 1803

Highlight(yellow) - 10. Why Should You Invest? > Page 115 · Location 1827 why you should invest: To save for your future self. To preserve your money against inflation. To replace your human capital with financial capital. 翻译： 为什么要投资：为未来的自己储蓄。保护你的资金免受通货膨胀的影响。用金融资本取代你的人力资本。

Highlight(yellow) - 10. Why Should You Invest? > Page 118 · Location 1871 with an inflation rate of 5% annually, purchasing power is halved every 14 years. 翻译： 如果通货膨胀率每年为 5%，购买力每 14 年就会减半。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 127 · Location 2020 It is this highly volatile nature of stocks that makes them difficult to hold during turbulent times. Seeing a decade’s worth of growth disappear in a matter of days can be gut-wrenching even for the most seasoned investors. 翻译： 正是股票这种高度波动性的特性，使得它们在动荡时期难以持有。即使对于经验最丰富的投资者来说，看到十年积累的增长在几天内消失，也会让人感到心痛。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 127 · Location 2023 The best way to combat such emotional volatility is to focus on the long term. While this does not guarantee returns, the evidence of history suggests that, with enough time, stocks tend to make up for their periodic losses. Time is an equity investor’s friend. 翻译： 对抗这种情绪波动性的最佳方法是专注于长期。虽然这不能保证回报，但历史的证据表明，只要有足够的时间，股票往往会弥补它们周期性的损失。时间是股票投资者的朋友。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 128 · Location 2041 Stocks Summary Average compounded annual return: 8%–10%. Pros: High historic returns. Easy to own and trade. Low maintenance (someone else runs the business). Cons: High volatility. Valuations can change quickly based on sentiment rather than fundamentals. 翻译： 股票 总结：平均复合年化回报率：8%–10%。优点：历史回报率高。易于拥有和交易。维护成本低（别人运营业务）。缺点：波动性高。估值可能根据情绪而非基本面迅速变化。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 130 · Location 2076 Why You Should/ Shouldn’t Invest in Bonds I recommend bonds because of these characteristics: Bonds tend to rise when stocks (and other risky assets) fall. Bonds have a more consistent income stream than other assets. Bonds can provide liquidity to rebalance your portfolio or cover liabilities. 翻译： 为什么你应该/不应该投资债券：我推荐债券是因为这些特性：当股票（和其他风险资产）下跌时，债券往往会上涨。债券比其他资产拥有更稳定的收入流。债券可以提供流动性来再平衡你的投资组合或覆盖负债。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 133 · Location 2113 Bonds Summary Average compounded annual return: 2%–4% (can approach 0% in a low-rate environment). Pros: Lower volatility. Good for rebalancing. Safety of principal. Cons: Low returns, especially after inflation. Not great for income in a low-yield environment. 翻译： 债券 总结：平均复合年化回报率：2%–4%（在低利率环境下可接近 0%）。优点：波动性较低。适合再平衡。本金安全。缺点：回报率低，尤其是在通胀之后。在低收益环境下，收入表现不佳。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 136 · Location 2156 Investment Property Summary Average compounded annual return: 12%–15% (dependent on local rental conditions). Pros: Higher returns than other more traditional asset classes, especially when using leverage. Cons: Managing the property and tenants can be a headache. Hard to diversify. 翻译： 投资房产 总结：平均复合年化回报率：12%–15%（取决于当地租赁条件）。优点：比其他更传统的资产类别回报率更高，尤其是在使用杠杆时。缺点：管理房产和租户可能令人头疼。难以分散投资。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 138 · Location 2199 REITs Summary Average compounded annual return: 10%–12%. Pros: Real estate exposure that you don’t have to manage. Less correlated with stocks during good times. Cons: Volatility greater than or equal to stocks. Less liquidity for non-traded REITs. Highly correlated with stocks and other risk assets during stock market crashes. 翻译： 房地产投资信托基金 (REITs) 总结：平均复合年化回报率：10%–12%。优点：获得房地产敞口而无需自己管理。在市场好时与股票的相关性较低。缺点：波动性大于或等于股票。非交易型 REITs 的流动性较低。在股市崩盘期间与股票和其他风险资产高度相关。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 142 · Location 2278 Small Business Summary Average compounded annual return: 20%–25%, but expect lots of losers. Pros: Can have extremely outsized returns. The more involved you are, the more future opportunities you will see. Cons: Huge time commitment. Lots of failures can be discouraging. 翻译： 小型企业 总结：平均复合年化回报率：20%–25%，但要预期有很多失败者。优点：可以获得极高的回报。你参与得越多，未来能看到的机会就越多。缺点：巨大的时间投入。许多失败可能会令人气馁。

Highlight(yellow) - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 147 · Location 2351 What About Gold, Crypto, Art, Etc? A handful of asset classes did not make the above list for the simple reason that they don’t produce income. Gold, cryptocurrency, commodities, art, and wine have no reliable income stream associated with their ownership, so I have not included them in my list of income-producing assets. Of course, this does not mean that you can’t make money with these assets. What it does mean is that their valuations are based solely on perception—what someone else is willing to pay for them. Without underlying cash flows, perception is everything. 翻译： 那黄金、加密货币、艺术品等呢？少数资产类别没有出现在上述列表中，原因很简单：它们不产生收入。黄金、加密货币、大宗商品、艺术品和葡萄酒在其所有权方面没有可靠的收入流，因此我没有将它们纳入我的产生收入的资产清单中。当然，这并不意味着你不能用这些资产赚钱。它意味着它们的估值完全基于感知——即别人愿意为它们支付多少。没有潜在的现金流，感知就是一切。 Note - 11. What Should You Invest In? > Page 147 · Location 2357 没有现金流 翻译： 没有现金流

Highlight(yellow) - 12. Why You Shouldn’t Buy Individual Stocks > Page 150 · Location 2456 Why You Shouldn’t Buy Individual Stocks 翻译： 为什么你不应该购买个股

Highlight(yellow) - 12. Why You Shouldn’t Buy Individual Stocks > Page 151 · Location 2487 The mental turmoil. The fear of missing out. The elation, triumph, pain, and regret. It was all perfectly packaged into a single two-hour window. Battling emotions is just the tip of the stock picking iceberg. I know because I used to pick stocks years ago as well. In addition to the emotional difficulties, you also have to deal with periods of underperformance and the possibility that you don’t actually have any stock picking skill. 翻译： 精神上的动荡。害怕错失（FOMO）。欣喜、胜利、痛苦和遗憾。所有这些都被完美地打包在一个两小时的窗口期内。与情绪搏斗只是选股冰山一角。我知道这一点，因为多年前我也曾选股。除了情感上的困难之外，你还必须应对表现不佳的时期，以及你可能根本没有选股技能的可能性。

Highlight(yellow) - 12. Why You Shouldn’t Buy Individual Stocks > Page 157 · Location 2576 “The very best way to learn about the dangers of individual stock investing is to familiarize yourself with the basics of finance and the empirical literature. But if you can’t do that, then, sure, what you have to do is put 5% or 10% of your money into individual stocks. And make sure you rigorously calculate your return, your annualized return, and then ask yourself, ‘Could I have done better just by buying a total stock market index fund?’” 82 翻译： “了解个股投资危险的最佳方法是熟悉金融基础知识和实证文献。但如果你做不到，那么，当然，你必须将 5% 或 10% 的资金投入个股。并确保你严格计算你的回报率、你的年化回报率，然后问自己：‘仅仅购买一个整体股票市场指数基金，我是否可以做得更好？’” 82

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 161 · Location 2649 Most stock markets go up most of the time. This is true despite the chaotic and sometimes destructive course of human history. As Warren Buffett so eloquently stated: “In the 20th century, the United States endured two world wars and other traumatic and expensive military conflicts; the Depression; a dozen or so recessions and financial panics; oil shocks; a flu epidemic; and the resignation of a disgraced president. Yet the Dow rose from 66 to 11,497.” 翻译： 大多数股票市场大部分时间都在上涨。尽管人类历史的进程是混乱且有时是破坏性的，但这是事实。正如沃伦·巴菲特雄辩地所说：“在 20 世纪，美国经历了两次世界大战和其他创伤性且代价高昂的军事冲突；大萧条；十几次衰退和金融恐慌；石油冲击；流感疫情；以及一位失势总统的辞职。然而，道琼斯指数从 66 上涨到了 11,497。”

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 161 · Location 2658 Given this empirical evidence, it suggests that you should invest your money as soon as possible. Why is this? Because most markets going up most of the time means that every day you end up waiting to invest usually means higher prices you will have to pay in the future. So, instead of waiting for the best time to get invested, you should just take the plunge and invest what you can now. 翻译： 鉴于这些实证证据，它表明你应该尽快投资你的资金。为什么是这样？因为大多数市场大部分时间都在上涨，这意味着你每天等待投资，通常意味着你未来必须支付更高的价格。因此，不要等待最佳时机进行投资，你应该果断行动，现在就投资你能投入的资金。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 161 · Location 2664 Imagine you have been gifted $ 1 million and you want to grow it as much as possible over the next 100 years. However, you can only undertake one of two possible investment strategies. You must either: Invest all your cash now, or Invest 1% of your cash each year for the next 100 years. Which would you prefer? If we assume that the assets you are investing in will increase in value over time (otherwise why would you be investing?), then it should be clear that buying now will be better than buying over the course of 100 years. Waiting a century to get invested means buying at ever higher prices while your uninvested cash also loses value to inflation. 翻译： 想象一下，你获得了一百万美元，你想在接下来的 100 年内尽可能多地增长它。然而，你只能采用两种可能的投资策略之一。你必须：现在投资所有现金，或者在接下来的 100 年里每年投资 1% 的现金。你会选择哪一个？如果我们假设你所投资的资产会随时间增值（否则你为什么要投资呢？），那么很明显，现在购买会比在 100 年内分批购买更好。等待一个世纪才开始投资，意味着你将以不断上涨的价格购买，而你未投资的现金也会因通货膨胀而贬值。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 162 · Location 2676 “The best time to start was yesterday. The next best time is today.” 翻译： “最好的开始时间是昨天。其次最好的时间就是今天。”

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 163 · Location 2684 Why Better Prices in the Future are Likely (And Why You Shouldn’t Wait for Them) 翻译： 为什么未来更有可能出现更好的价格（以及为什么你不应该等待它们）

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 176 · Location 2909 If you think that the market is overvalued and due for a major pullback, you may need to wait years, if ever, before you are vindicated. Consider this before you use valuation as an excuse to stay in cash. 翻译： 如果你认为市场被高估了，即将迎来重大回调，你可能需要等待数年，甚至永远等待，才能得到证明。在用估值作为留在现金中的借口之前，请考虑这一点。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 176 · Location 2911 Final Summary When deciding between investing all your money now or over time, it is almost always better to invest it now. This is true across all asset classes, time periods, and nearly all valuation regimes. Generally, the longer you wait to deploy your capital, the worse off you will be. 翻译： 最终总结：当决定是现在投资所有资金还是分批投资时，几乎总是现在投资更好。这适用于所有资产类别、时间周期和几乎所有估值模式。一般来说，你等待部署资本的时间越长，你的处境就会越差。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 177 · Location 2915 I say generally because the only time when you are better off by averaging-in over time is while the market is crashing. However, it is precisely when the market is crashing that you will be the least enthusiastic to invest. 翻译： 我说“一般来说”，是因为只有在市场崩盘时，通过分批平均投入（averaging-in）才更有利。然而，正是在市场崩盘时，你最不情愿去投资。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 177 · Location 2917 It is difficult to fight off these emotions, which is why many investors won’t be able to keep buying as the market falls anyways. 翻译： 很难抵抗这些情绪，这就是为什么许多投资者在市场下跌时将无法持续买入。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 177 · Location 2919 If you are still worried about investing a large sum of money right now, the problem may be that you’re considering a portfolio that is too risky for your liking. What’s the solution to this? Invest your money now into a more conservative portfolio than you normally would. 翻译： 如果你仍然担心现在投入一大笔钱，问题可能是你考虑的投资组合对你来说风险太高了。解决方案是什么？现在将你的资金投入到比你通常选择的更保守的投资组合中。

Highlight(yellow) - 13. How Soon Should You Invest? > Page 177 · Location 2921 If your target allocation is a 80/ 20 stock/ bond portfolio, you might want to consider investing it all into a 60/ 40 stock/ bond portfolio and transitioning it over time. 翻译： 如果你的目标配置是 80/20 的股票/债券组合，你可能想考虑将其全部投入到 60/40 的股票/债券组合中，并随着时间进行过渡。

Highlight(yellow) - 14. Why You Shouldn’t Wait to Buy the Dip > Page 178 · Location 2939 14. Why You Shouldn’t Wait to Buy the Dip Even God couldn’t beat dollar-cost averaging 翻译： 14. 为什么你不应该等待抄底（Buy the Dip） 即使是上帝也无法击败美元成本平均法

Highlight(yellow) - 14. Why You Shouldn’t Wait to Buy the Dip > Page 179 · Location 2961 Why is this true? Because buying the dip only works when you know that a severe decline is coming and you can time it perfectly. 翻译： 为什么这是真的？因为只有当你知道一次严重的下跌即将来临，并且你能完美地把握时机时，抄底才有效。

Highlight(yellow) - 14. Why You Shouldn’t Wait to Buy the Dip > Page 179 · Location 2962 The problem is that severe market declines don’t happen too often. In U.S. market history severe dips have only taken place in the 1930s, 1970s, and 2000s. That’s rare. This means that Buy the Dip only has a small chance of beating DCA. 翻译： 问题在于，严重的市场下跌并不经常发生。在美国市场的历史上，严重的下跌只发生在 1930 年代、1970 年代和 2000 年代。这非常罕见。这意味着抄底只有很小的机会能击败 DCA（美元成本平均法）。

Highlight(yellow) - 14. Why You Shouldn’t Wait to Buy the Dip > Page 189 · Location 3050 You should invest as soon and as often as you can. 翻译： 你应该尽可能早、尽可能频繁地投资。

Highlight(yellow) - 16. Why You Shouldn’t Fear Volatility > Page 204 · Location 3269 How much would the market have to decline in the next year for you to forgo investing in stocks altogether to invest in bonds instead? 翻译： 在未来一年中，市场需要下跌多少，你才会完全放弃投资股票而转而投资债券呢？

Highlight(yellow) - 16. Why You Shouldn’t Fear Volatility > Page 208 · Location 3308 The answer is 15% and above. 翻译： 答案是 15% 及以上。

Highlight(yellow) - 16. Why You Shouldn’t Fear Volatility > Page 212 · Location 3341 “If you’re not willing to react with equanimity to a market price decline of 50% two or three times a century, you’re not fit to be a common shareholder and you deserve the mediocre result you’re going to get.” 翻译： “如果你不愿意以泰然自若的态度来应对市场价格下跌 50% 的情况，即使是两到三次一个世纪，那么你就不适合成为一名普通股东，你理应得到平庸的结果。”

Highlight(yellow) - 17. How to Buy During a Crisis > Page 221 · Location 3457 As you can see, when U.S. equity markets have gotten cut in half, the future annualized returns usually exceed 25%. This implies that when the market is down by 50%, it’s time to back up the truck and invest as much as you can afford. Of course, you may not have a lot of investable cash to take advantage of these rare occurrences when the market is in turmoil, because of wider economic uncertainty. However, if you do have the cash to spare then the data suggests that it would be wise to take advantage of this buying opportunity. 翻译： 正如你所看到的，当美国股票市场下跌一半时，未来的年化回报通常超过 25%。这意味着当市场下跌 50% 时，是时候“装满卡车”并投资你能承受的尽可能多的资金了。当然，由于更广泛的经济不确定性，你可能没有足够的可投资现金来利用这些市场动荡时出现的罕见机会。但是，如果你有闲置的现金，那么数据表明利用这个买入机会是明智的。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 226 · Location 3523 When Should You Sell? On rebalancing, concentrated positions, and the purpose of investing 翻译： 何时卖出？关于再平衡、集中持仓和投资的目的

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 226 · Location 3530 fear of missing out on the upside and the fear of losing money on the downside. This emotional vice can make you question every investment decision that you make. 翻译： 害怕错过上涨机会（FOMO）和害怕下跌时亏损。这种情感上的恶习可能会让你质疑你所做的每一个投资决策。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 226 · Location 3532 To avoid this mental turmoil, you should come up with a set of conditions under which you would sell beforehand instead of relying on your emotional state when you are thinking of getting out of a position. This will allow you to sell your investments on your own terms, to a predefined plan. After coming up with a list of reasons myself, I can only find three cases under which you should consider selling an investment: To rebalance. To get out of a concentrated (or losing) position. To meet your financial needs. If you aren’t rebalancing your portfolio, getting out of a concentrated (or losing) position, or trying to meet a financial need, then I see no reason to sell an investment—ever. 翻译： 为了避免这种精神上的动荡，你应该事先制定一套条件，在考虑退出某个头寸时，而不是依赖你的情绪状态来决定卖出。这将使你能够按照自己的条件，按照预定的计划来出售你的投资。在我自己列出了一系列原因之后，我只能找到三种你应该考虑出售投资的情况：进行再平衡。退出集中（或亏损）头寸。满足你的财务需求。如果你没有再平衡你的投资组合、没有退出集中（或亏损）头寸，或者没有试图满足财务需求，那么我认为就没有理由出售投资——永远没有理由。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 227 · Location 3546 it’s usually better to buy immediately rather than over time. The reasoning was simple: since most markets go up most of the time, waiting to buy usually means losing out on upside. When it comes to selling an asset, we can use the same set of reasoning, but come to the opposite conclusion. Since markets tend to go up over time, the optimal thing to do is to sell as late as possible. Therefore, selling over time (or as late as possible) is usually better than selling right away. 翻译： 通常来说，立即买入比分批买入更好。理由很简单：由于大多数市场大部分时间都在上涨，等待买入通常意味着错失了上涨的机会。当涉及到出售资产时，我们可以使用相同的推理，但得出相反的结论。由于市场倾向于随时间上涨，最佳做法是尽可能晚地卖出。因此，分批出售（或尽可能晚地出售）通常比立即出售更好。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 227 · Location 3553 buy quickly, but sell slowly. 翻译： 快速买入，缓慢卖出。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 228 · Location 3559 What’s Rebalancing Good for Anyways? “Perfectly balanced, as all things should be.” 翻译： 再平衡到底有什么好处？“完美平衡，正如万物应有的那样。”

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 231 · Location 3593 Given that rebalancing doesn’t typically enhance returns, why do people still do it? To reduce risk. 翻译： 考虑到再平衡通常不会提高回报，人们为什么仍然这样做？是为了降低风险。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 234 · Location 3629 result, I recommend an annual rebalance for two reasons: It takes less time. It coincides with our annual tax season. 翻译： 结果，我推荐每年进行一次再平衡，原因有两个：它耗时较少。它与我们的年度纳税季相吻合。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 234 · Location 3642 Whatever you decide to do when it comes to rebalancing frequency, avoiding unnecessary taxation is a must. This is why I don’t recommend rebalancing frequently in your taxable accounts (i.e., brokerage account). Because every time you do, you have to pay Uncle Sam. 翻译： 无论你决定如何进行再平衡频率，避免不必要的税务是必须的。这就是为什么我不建议在你的应税账户（即经纪账户）中频繁进行再平衡。因为你每次做的时候，都得向“山姆大叔”（指美国政府）缴税。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 235 · Location 3647 While selling an asset to rebalance isn’t the worst thing in the world, there is a way to rebalance your portfolio that involves no tax consequences at all—Just Keep Buying. That’s right. You can buy your way back into a rebalanced portfolio. I call this an accumulation rebalance because you are rebalancing by buying your most underweight asset over time. 翻译： 虽然为了再平衡而出售资产不是最糟糕的事情，但有一种方法可以实现投资组合的再平衡，而完全没有税务后果——那就是“持续买入”。没错。你可以通过买入的方式重新进入一个再平衡的投资组合。我称之为“积累式再平衡”，因为你是在随着时间推移买入你权重最低的资产来进行再平衡的。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 239 · Location 3707 The point is that underperformance is inevitable and not a good reason to sell. 翻译： 重点是，表现不佳是不可避免的，而不是一个好的卖出理由。

Highlight(yellow) - 18. When Should You Sell? > Page 240 · Location 3719 Fund the life you need before you risk it for the life you want. 翻译： 在将它冒险用于你想要的生命之前，先为你需要的生活提供资金。

Highlight(yellow) - 20. Why You Will Never Feel Rich > Page 261 · Location 4053 Why You Will Never Feel Rich And why you probably already are 翻译： 你永远不会觉得自己是富翁，以及你可能已经如此的原因

Highlight(yellow) - 21. The Most Important Asset > Page 272 · Location 4217 The Most Important Asset And why you’ll never get any more of it 翻译： 最重要的资产，以及为什么你永远不会再得到更多它

item.title: 一把梭哈还是逐步买入？
item.description: 探讨尽早投资的优势，结合历史数据分析和风险考量，给出适合不同投资者的建议。
item.content:encoded:
大多数股票市场大部分时间都在上涨

包含世界大战期间,与 COVID-19 期间
Most stock markets go up most of the time.

虽然感觉我们总是处于市场崩盘的风口浪尖，但事实是，重大崩盘非常罕见。这就是为什么 Average-In 在历史上的大部分时间里都表现不佳的原因。

最好的开始时间是昨天

下一个最佳时间是今天。 The best time to start was yesterday. The next best time is today.

  • If we assume that the assets you are investing in will increase in value over time (otherwise why would you be investing?), then it should be clear that buying now will be better than buying over the course of 100 years. Waiting a century to get invested means buying at ever higher prices while your uninvested cash also loses value to inflation.
  • 如果我们假设你所投资的资产会随着时间的推移而增值（否则你为什么要投资？），那么应该很清楚，现在购买将比在 100 年内购买更好。等待一个世纪才能获得投资意味着以更高的价格购买，而您未投资的现金也会因通货膨胀而失去价值。

为什么未来可能会有更好的价格

每 20 个交易日（每月一个）中就有 1 个交易日将为您提供绝对便宜的价格。其他 19 个会让你在未来的某个时候感到买家的懊悔。 这就是为什么感觉等待更低的价格是正确的做法。从技术上讲，你有 95% 的机会是对的。

为什么你不应该等待

有时永远不会出现较低的价格，或者您必须等待很长时间才能看到这个较低的价格。 最关键的是，你无法 timing 市场，你不知道什么时候价格是更好的。因为更好是相对概念

虽然感觉我们总是处于市场崩盘的风口浪尖，但事实是，重大崩盘非常罕见。这就是为什么 Average-In 在历史上的大部分时间里都表现不佳的原因。

为什么 2008 年 8 月“立即购买”相对于平均收入的表现如此糟糕？

因为美国股市在 2008 年 8 月后不久就崩盘了。更具体地说，如果您在 2008 年 8 月底向标准普尔 500 指数投资了 12,000 美元，到 2009 年 8 月底，您将只有 9,810 美元（包括再投资股息），总损失为 18.25%。

不过，从这张图表中真正可以看出的不是这个峰值，而是这条线通常低于 0%。如果该线低于 0%，则 Average-In 的表现低于 Buy Now，而在 0% 以上时，Average-In 的表现优于 Buy Now。

如您所见，大多数时候，Average-In 的表现低于 Buy Now。这不仅仅是新近偏见。如果我们看一下 1920 年以来的美国股票回报率，我们会发现，在每个滚动的 12 个月期间，平均表现比“立即购买”低 4.5%，在所有滚动的 12 个月期间，平均表现比“立即购买”低 4.5%。下图以与上一个图表相同的方式说明了这个较长的时间段。

风险呢？

高收益必然带来高风险，用更大的回撤可能来赌 4%的收益，这值得吗？

但是，如果您担心风险，那么也许您应该考虑遵循“立即购买”策略并投资于更保守的投资组合。

However, if you are worried about risk, then maybe you should consider following the Buy Now strategy and investing into a more conservative portfolio instead.

例如，如果您最初打算平均投资 100% 的股票投资组合，您可以按照“立即购买”策略进入 60/40 的股票/债券投资组合，以便在相同风险水平下获得稍高的回报。

For example, if originally you were going to Average-In to a 100% stock portfolio, you could follow the Buy Now strategy into a 60/40 stock/bond portfolio to have slightly better returns for the same level of risk.

如果您认为市场被高估并即将出现大幅回调，您可能需要等待数年，如果有的话，才能被证明是正确的。在您以估值为借口保留现金之前，请考虑这一点。

If you think that the market is overvalued and due for a major pullback, you may need to wait years, if ever, before you are vindicated. Consider this before you use valuation as an excuse to stay in cash.

最后总结

在决定现在投资所有资金还是随着时间的推移投资时，现在投资几乎总是更好。这适用于所有资产类别、时间段和几乎所有估值制度。一般来说，您等待部署资金的时间越长，您的情况就越糟。

我之所以这么说，是因为随着时间的推移，你唯一能通过平均入场而变得更好的时候是市场崩盘的时候。然而，恰恰是当市场崩盘时，您将最不热衷于投资。

所有人都疯狂的卖出，你不知道市场会跌到什么地步。

你很难抵制这些情绪，这就是为什么许多投资者无论如何都无法在市场下跌时继续买入的原因。

AI 答疑

作者的核心观点是：股市大多数时间都在上涨，因此尽早投资比分散投资更好，因为等待通常意味着错过上涨的机会。历史数据显示，平均成本法在大多数时间里（76%到 82%的 12 个月期）表现不如一次性投资，尤其是在市场总体向上的情况下。即使短期内可能会有更低的价格出现，但从长期来看，尽早进入市场的收益更大。

作者论点的合理之处

数据支持

  • 作者提供了充分的历史数据支持其论点
  • 跨越多个资产类别和时间周期的分析显示一次性买入确实平均收益更高
  • 即使在高估值时期，一次性买入仍然统计上占优

理论基础

  • 市场长期向上的特性确实支持尽早投资的逻辑
  • 通过调整资产配置来控制风险是合理的建议

作者论点的局限性

心理因素未充分考虑

  • 投资决策不仅仅是数学和统计的问题
  • 一次性投入大额资金的心理压力可能导致投资者在市场下跌时做出错误决策
  • 定投的价值之一是帮助投资者建立良好的投资习惯和心理韧性

个人情况的差异

  • 不同投资者的风险承受能力不同
  • 收入来源的稳定性会影响投资策略的选择
  • 投资目标和时间跨度的差异也应该被考虑

现实情况的复杂性

  • 真实市场环境比历史数据更复杂
  • 宏观经济环境、政策变化等因素都可能影响策略效果
  • 过去的表现不能完全预测未来

建议的平衡观点

策略组合

  • 可以考虑将一次性买入和定投结合使用
  • 比如将部分资金一次性投入，同时保持定期投资的习惯
  • 这样既能获得早期投资的优势，又能维持投资纪律

因人制宜

  • 根据个人具体情况选择合适的策略
  • 考虑自己的风险承受能力、投资经验和财务目标
  • 选择能让自己安心的投资方式更重要

动态调整

  • 定期评估和调整投资策略
  • 根据市场环境和个人情况的变化做出适当调整
  • 保持灵活性和适应性

结论

作者的分析从数据和理论角度来看是有说服力的，但投资决策不应该仅仅基于历史数据。每个投资者都需要找到适合自己的方式，在理性分析和心理承受能力之间取得平衡。定投虽然可能在纯收益角度稍逊一筹，但其降低心理压力、培养投资习惯的价值也不应被忽视。

item.title: 储蓄是为穷人，投资是为富人。
item.description: 不同阶段做不同的事，没钱的时候先卖力气搞钱，别想些没用的。
item.content:encoded:
• 首先，确定你预计在未来一年内能舒适地储蓄多少。
  • 其次，确定你预计你的投资在未来一年内能增长多少。
  • 最后，比较这两个数字。是你的预期储蓄更高，还是你的预期投资增长更高？

如果你的预期储蓄更高，那么你需要将更多精力放在储蓄和增加投资上。然而，如果你的预期投资增长更高，那么你应该花更多时间思考如何投资你已有的资金。如果这两个数字相近，那么你应该同时关注两者。
